newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says peace will go on despite settlement.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says peace will go on despite settlement.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday he was convinced peace moves with the PLO would continue despite the start of work on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Asked at a news conference if the construction would end the peace process, Netanyahu said: "Absolutely not. And I recommend to all parties concerned to stop this hyperbole...I'm sure the peace process will continue."

Netanyahu urged the Palestinian leadership not to incite violence over his right-wing government's plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim, a pine-covered hilltop which Israel calls Har Homa.
He said the Palestinians must decide "do they want terror or do they want peace"? Israel, he said, would not "sacrifice" Jerusalem, a city Israel claims as its capital.

Going on the offensive, Netanyahu said the Palestinian Authority had recently released from jail members of Hamas, a militant Islamic group responsible for suicide bombings that killed 59 people in Israel last year.

"I am saying that our intelligence shows very clearly, unmistakably that the Palestininan leadership has given the green light to the worst terrorist organisations in the world to go ahead with the kind of bus bombings and suicide attacks -- the kind of mass killings that brought a halt to the peace process," he said.
